title: Food 4
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. Three predecessors own 81 words — a1_food (35), a1_food_2 (23), a2_food (23) — covering every ingredient a beginner names, the four cooking verbs (grill, boil, bake, fry), and the restaurant basics (menu, bill, order, chef, serve). The sweep dropped season, eat out, organic, preservative, allergy and vegetarian as already taught. What is left is the layer between knowing the words and being able to cook or eat with someone: the verbs a recipe actually uses (marinate, simmer, whisk, grate, knead), how a meal is structured and talked about (starter, main course, side dish, helping, portion, leftovers, comfort food, acquired taste), and what is on the label (ingredient, processed, additive, shelf life, best before, gluten-free, nutrient, calorie, food waste). bland and savoury are in on purpose: a B2 student can say delicious and spicy but has no word for food that is simply dull, and none for the sweet/savoury split that English makes and Czech does not. C57 card 0 recaps Food 1 to 3. C49 all 36 across three boards of 12. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Food 1, 2 and 3 gave you the ingredients and the basics — bread, cheese, meat, rice, soup, salad, fruit, vegetable, menu, bill, order, grill, boil, bake, fry, chef, recipe, taste, spicy, fresh, serve. Those carry the sentences here. What is new is what a recipe actually tells you to do, how a meal is talked about, and what it says on the back of the packet.
cards.note_cz: Food 1, 2 a 3 ti daly suroviny a základ — bread, cheese, meat, rice, soup, salad, fruit, vegetable, menu, bill, order, grill, boil, bake, fry, chef, recipe, taste, spicy, fresh, serve. Ta slova nesou zdejší věty. Nové je to, co ti recept doopravdy říká dělat, jak se o jídle mluví a co stojí vzadu na obalu.

cards.title: Sweet or savoury
points: English splits food into **sweet** and **savoury**. Czech has no single word for the second.
**bland** is the word for food with no taste — not *not tasty*, which sounds like a complaint about the cook.

rows: salty rather than sweet — soup, cheese, meat
you have to learn to like it
what you eat when you need cheering up
